text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Baghdad to violate no-fly zone, U.S. pledges appropriate response. Iraq says it is sending helicopters to pick up returning Moslem pilgrims from Saudi Arabia's border area despite ban by United States and other Western powers on Iraqi flights in area.
- Kuwait's Interior Ministry denies local media report about Satanists group arrest.
- Results of seismic survey show more oil in Kuwait. State-owned Kuwait Oil Co is running $131 million survey aimed at discovering more oil and gas reserves.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange index rises 33.3 points to 2,269.2.
- United Arab Emirates branch of Kuwait's al-Ahli Bank reports $4.3 million profit in 1996, rise of 7.3 percent compared to 1995.
- U.S. wrestler faces trial on Tuesday on charges of assaulting Kuwait television presenter during live interview earlier in April.
- Four women storm police station and attack two security officers for unknown reasons.
